item.title: Vertical Speaker Cut With Captions

exact_text: Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.

turns.text: Make this 9:16 with her centred and add readable English captions matching what she says. Keep the whole 10 seconds and her original voice. Put the captions below her face.

item.tests: Tests portrait reframing combined with accurate, synchronized, readable burned-in speech captions.

answer_sheet.Source and subject: Use talk-one.mp4, keeping the woman centred.
answer_sheet.Size and duration: 9:16 vertical, the full 10 seconds; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Caption wording and language: English: Hi everyone! Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.
answer_sheet.Caption appearance: Your call on font and styling; use readable, high-contrast captions below her face, inside the frame, in short timed chunks.
answer_sheet.Audio: Keep her original voice and sound, with no replacement narration or added music.

must_haves: The output is a 9:16 edit of the attached footage, with the woman centred and her face fully visible.
The full 10 seconds and original voice are preserved in sync.
Visible captions reproduce 'Hi everyone! Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.' in order, with no omitted or invented words.
Captions appear in short readable chunks timed to the corresponding speech rather than displaying the entire transcript throughout.
Captions have clear contrast, stay fully within the frame and do not cover her face.

turns.text: Could you edit this clip with the woman kept centred? I’m a little worried the captions might distract from her rather than help people follow along. As far as the format and timing go, make it 9:16 and keep the whole 10 seconds. Please keep her original voice, too. Add readable English captions matching what she says, and put them below her face.

dialog.agent:
I’d use simple white English captions with a thin dark outline, positioned below her face—no bouncing text or word-by-word highlighting.

I can add captions while preserving her original voice and the full 10 seconds. However, the available caption tool can’t crop to 9:16 or keep her centred, and I wouldn’t use generative editing that could change her appearance or speech.

Is the attached clip already centred and 9:16? If not, please upload a centred 9:16 crop so I can caption it without altering her.
dialog.why: It asks whether the clip is already centred and 9:16, and requests a cropped upload if not, waiting for user input before proceeding.
dialog.user: I can’t confirm whether talk-one.mp4 is already centred and 9:16; that’s the source clip I want to use, with the woman kept centred in the final vertical edit. The captions should read, “Hi everyone! Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.” Your suggested caption styling sounds fine, and free-tier resolution is fine too.

dialog.agent:
Thanks—the caption text and styling are clear. The target is **9:16, the woman centred, all 10 seconds, and her original voice**, at free-tier resolution.

I’m blocked on the reframing: the connected tools don’t offer a reliable crop-and-centre operation. The subtitle tool also transcribes audio automatically; it doesn’t accept your sentence as an exact caption override.

I haven’t started a job or spent credits. I can make a **captions-only version** with simple outlined white text below her face, but it would retain the source framing and use automatic transcription. Would you like that partial version?
dialog.why: It asks whether the user wants a captions-only partial version and waits for their choice, while explaining the tool limitations.
dialog.user: Yes, please go ahead with the captions-only version using talk-one.mp4 and automatic transcription. Keep the full 10 seconds and her original voice and sound, with the captions below her face inside the frame. I’m still a little worried about captions distracting from her, so the simple, readable styling you suggested sounds good.

turns.agent:
The captioning attempt was blocked by **insufficient Magic Hour credits**, so no edited video was created.

You’ll need to add credits or wait for a credit refresh before I can make the approved captions-only version: all 10 seconds, original voice and sound, and simple outlined white captions at the bottom of the frame.
